title: Agent-harness vendors ship gVisor+OS-sandbox+VM containment specs by Q2 2027
body: Anthropic published How we contain Claude across products on its engineering blog Saturday May 30, walking through the agent-isolation stack converged across all three product surfaces: gVisor containers with seccomp syscall filtering on isolated infrastructure for Claude.ai (ephemeral per-session filesystems), OS-native process sandboxes for Claude Code (Seatbelt on macOS and Bubblewrap on Linux, with an 84% reduction in permission prompts after delegating command approvals to a model-based classifier), and full guest VMs for Claude Cowork running on Apple Virtualization framework on macOS and Hyper-V HCS on Windows with host-held credentials and read-only / read-write / read-write-no-delete file-mount modes. The structural force is procurement-side. Once one frontier lab publicly commits to mature hypervisor + OS-sandbox + VM containment as the named posture and explicitly argues that the software you build yourself is often the weakest component, every peer agent-harness vendor faces a buyer-side question whose answer cannot stay opaque: does your harness ship equivalent containment, or do you document why not. The same convergence pressure that pulled SBOM formats and hyperscaler responsible-scaling templates into a small number of public shapes will act here, because enterprise security teams refuse to map N vendor-specific harness-isolation narratives into N risk-acceptance frameworks when the reference design is already public. By Q2 2027 we expect at least two of Cursor, Codex CLI, Cline, Windsurf, Devin, and Continue to publish named containment profiles matching the Anthropic posture (per-OS sandbox tier for the local CLI plus per-product VM tier for the autonomous-agent surface), and at least one standards body (OpenSSF, the CNCF agent SIG, or a Frontier Model Forum working group analog) to publish a draft agent-runtime-containment profile that names gVisor or equivalent at the cloud tier and named OS sandboxes at the laptop tier as the reference design. Bear case is a single peer vendor publishes a divergent containment spec (Wasm-only or eBPF-only) that fragments the convergence pressure before two named vendors align; absent that fragmentation, Q2 2027 lands the first peer-vendor containment specs and the first standards-body draft naming hypervisor + OS sandbox as the agent-runtime reference.

reasoning.because: Anthropic published gVisor + Seatbelt/Bubblewrap + per-OS VM containment stack, 84% prompt cut
reasoning.given: One frontier lab publicly committing to hypervisor + OS sandbox forces peer harness vendors to match
reasoning.so_that: At least two peer coding-agent vendors publish containment specs and a standards body drafts a profile
reasoning.landing: By Q2 2027; two peer-vendor specs plus one standards-body draft
reasoning.plain_language: Anthropic published how it locks down its AI coding tools. Rival tool makers will copy the design and write shared safety rules.

summary: Anthropic published Claude.ai (gVisor+seccomp), Claude Code (Seatbelt/Bubblewrap, 84% fewer prompts), and Claude Cowork (Apple VZ + Windows HCS VMs) containment stack May 30. By Q2 2027 two peer agent-harness vendors publish matching specs and a standards body drafts a profile.
